correctness.rationale: Claim audited is the CORRECTED claim in DRAFT.md (M=17 unique ball), not the false assigned target (<=15). Every essential inference was re-verified independently. (1) Lower bound: B(S)={A:|A cap S|>=3} has size 1+C(4,3)*C(4,1)=17; hand proof |A cap B|>=|(A cap S) cap (B cap S)|>=3+3-4=2 is correct, so B(S) is 1-free; independently recomputed size 17 and zero bad pairs. (2) Star/clique size-15 1-free checks correct (star: contains fixed pair => inter>=2; clique in 6-set: |A union B|<=6 => inter>=2). (3) Shifting refutation correct under standard Frankl S_{i,j} definition: F={{2,3,4,5},{1,6,7,8}} has inter 0 (1-free) but S_{1,2}(F)={{1,3,4,5},{1,6,7,8}} has inter {1} size 1; recomputed with formal shift implementation. This invalidates the audit_plan shifting reduction, as DRAFT correctly states; monotone >=t preservation does not imply forbidden-value preservation. (4) Symmetry lemmas correct: S8 transitivity reduces to families containing 1234; Stab(1234)=S_{1..4}xS_{5..8} (576 perms) has exactly 3 orbits on compatible second sets, verified both by reasoning (fixed a=|B cap 1234| determines orbit) and by brute-force orbit computation (sizes 1,16,36 for a=0,3,2; a=1 excluded by 1-freeness with 1234, a=4 gives B=1234). Representatives 5678/1235/1256 correct; subpool sizes 36/42/40 and full pool 53 recomputed exactly. (5) Upper bound M<=17: candidate final_verify.py rerun passes (3 cases no-16-more, 267 nodes total, full-pool cross-check no-17-more). Pruning rules audited valid: popcount bound valid, isolated-vertex forcing valid (isolated v satisfies alpha(mask)=1+alpha(mask\{v})), greedy clique-cover bound valid (any clique contributes <=1 independent vertex, so partition count is UB), max-degree branching exhaustive. Independently re-proved with a different algorithm (Tomita-style Max-Clique with greedy coloring bound on compatibility graph): max-more in P=16 (79 nodes) and global max over 70 sets=17 (383 nodes), without assuming symmetry. (6) Uniqueness: candidate enumerate17.py rerun finds exactly 17 families containing 1234, one S8-orbit, all balls (0.0s). Independently re-enumerated with a different ordered-combination DFS (no coloring, no isolated forcing, no degree heuristic): exactly 17 solutions in 24809 nodes, all verified 1-free and all satisfy ball property; global distinct-ball count is 70 (one per center) with 17 containing 1234, matching predicted-count 17=17. Single-orbit follows from S8 transitivity on 4-sets (pi(B(S))=B(pi(S))). (7) Counting remark (convexity alone insufficient at m=18: N2+3N3>=156, N2+N3<=153 satisfiable) verified arithmetically (156=24*6+4*3 from 108 incidences over 28 pairs). No gaps: empty/singleton families trivial; a=4 second-set case vacuous. Computer-assisted part is exactly specified, stdlib-only, reruns in seconds with two independent search paths agreeing.

originality.rationale: Claim-level comparison on hypotheses, quantifiers, constants and scope: (1) Ellis et al. abstract retrieved live states equality g=f only for o(n)<=k<=n/2-o(n), excluding k=n/2; candidate k=4=n/2 with t=2 falls in the stated gap n/2-o(n)<k<n/2+t/2, so no implication of M=17. (2) Kupavskii-Zakharov abstract retrieved live requires t<=n^{1-eps} and n>n0(eps) asymptotic; it gives junta bounds with no small-n constant and no tie analysis at (8,4,1). (3) Frankl-Rodl 1987 Crossref metadata/abstract retrieved live concerns (2-eps)^n-type large-n bounds for forbidden [n/4] intersection and general partition patterns, with thresholds excluding n=8; it does not enumerate C(8,4)=70 or certify no-18. (4) Ahlswede-Khachatrian (Crossref DOI verified live) optimizes over t-intersecting (>=2) families where ball is already known; the candidate extends optimality to 1-free families that may use disjoint pairs (intersection 0), a strictly larger class — verified distinct because star/clique/ball examples in record use 0 and >=2 intersections, and convexity remark shows pair/triple counts alone do not close the bound. No retrieved source states the exact constant 17, the count of 17 extremal balls containing 1234 forming one S8-orbit, the three-orbit reduction (5678/1235/1256 with pools 36/42/40), or the shifting-invalidity counterexample 0->1 via S_{1,2}. Construction reuse of B(S) does not defeat originality because the optimality claim in the larger class plus uniqueness is new relative to all inspected abstracts/metadata. Therefore no source found substantively covers or implies the candidate.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later. Not a textbook restatement (textbook EKR/AK bounds are far from sharp here and give no 1-free optimum), not a mere parameter substitution (structural surprise: true optimum is neither star nor clique but a third type, ball, beating both 15>17 by 13% and collapsing the assumed two-extremal tie), not a tiny unmotivated gain (changes extremal structure from 2 types to 1 different type and corrects a false assigned claim that would otherwise propagate), and not an unexplained enumeration (human lemmas: transitivity + 3-orbit reduction + hand ball bound + shifting-counterexample pedagogy, plus exact certified B&B with auditable prunes, full-pool cross-check, and predicted-count match 17=17 for uniqueness). Additional durable value: explicit counterexample that Frankl shifts do not preserve forbidden intersections (prevents future invalid reductions) and demonstration that pair/triple convexity alone cannot close the bound. Scope is narrow (single (8,4,1) point, computer-assisted upper bound) but sharp, complete (exact max + uniqueness), and reproducible in seconds; honest limitations stated. Rejecting would perversely penalize correcting the false 15-target.
